# Reform UK Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Overview
The manifesto, titled "Our Contract with You," outlines policies across multiple areas with implementation targets beginning within 100 days of election. The document includes costings claiming £160 billion in annual savings and growth against £141 billion in costs.

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers. Foreign workers would face a 20% National Insurance rate (versus 13.8% for British workers), with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses. A five-year residency requirement would apply for benefits access. Student dependents would be barred, and foreign criminals would face immediate deportation.

## Economy
**Personal taxation:** Income tax threshold raised to £20,000, removing 7 million people from income tax. Inheritance tax abolished for estates under £2 million. Stamp duty reduced significantly.

**Business:** Corporation tax threshold raised to £100,000 profit minimum, with rates reduced from 25% to eventually 15%. VAT threshold increased to £150,000. Business rates abolished for high street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals. IR35 rules would be abolished.

## Public Spending
The manifesto proposes saving £91 billion annually through: stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion), 5% efficiency cuts across departments (£50 billion), and halving foreign aid (£6 billion).

## NHS
Frontline NHS staff would pay zero basic rate tax for three years. Private healthcare would receive 20% tax relief. A voucher scheme would allow NHS patients to access private treatment if waiting time targets are missed. Student fees would be written off for medical staff completing ten years of NHS service.

## Energy
Net Zero commitments would be scrapped, along with renewable energy subsidies. The party proposes fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licences, granting shale gas test licences, and developing small modular nuclear reactors. Environmental levies and VAT on energy bills would be removed.

## Policing and Justice
40,000 new frontline police officers would be recruited over five years. Automatic life sentences would apply for violent repeat offenders. 10,000 new detention places would be built. The definition of hate crime would be changed to require more than perception-based complaints.

## Education
The manifesto proposes curriculum changes requiring balanced teaching of historical topics, banning gender transitioning discussions in schools, and providing 20% tax relief on independent school fees. University undergraduate numbers would be restricted, and two-year degree options introduced.

## Defence
Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by year three, then 3% within six years. Military pay would be reviewed, and 30,000 full-time army recruits sought. A dedicated Veterans ministry would be established.

## Housing
Planning reform would fast-track brownfield development. Social housing would prioritise local residents. Section 24 landlord tax rules would be scrapped, and the Renters Reform Bill abolished.

## Constitutional Changes
Proposals include replacing the House of Lords with a smaller elected chamber, reforming postal voting, holding a referendum on proportional representation, and creating a British Bill of Rights. The BBC licence fee would be scrapped.

## Transport and Infrastructure
HS2 would be cancelled. ULEZ zones and low traffic neighbourhoods would be banned. Critical utilities would move to 50% public ownership with the remainder held by UK pension funds.

## Agriculture and Fishing
The farming budget would increase to £3 billion with focus on smaller farms. EU fishing vessels would require paid licences for UK waters, and supertrawlers would be banned.
